results.summary: The two drawn pins (the Yodelin lot and the summit) are already in the right places; the flagged problem was the approach distance field, not a pin.
results.evidence: Finding concerns dist_km (round-trip vs one-way), not coordinates. Pin 0 (Yodelin lot) 47.765955,-121.078176 sits ~150 m from the mapped Yodelin Ski Area parking (OSM 47.76708,-121.07698). Pin 6 (summit) 47.77044,-121.13302 matches the published peak coordinate exactly, and the USGS terrain at that point is 5,643 ft and is a local high point (all 8 neighbours 150-300 m away are lower), matching the stated 5,645-5,654 ft summit. Pins 1-5 have no coordinates and are not drawn. Nothing to move.
sources: https://overpass-api.de (OSM way 896898747 Yodelin Ski Area parking)

results.summary: The White Pass pin sat about 4 km north of the pass; it is moved onto the pass. The Boulder Basin camp pin is also misplaced (it sits high on the glacier) but no two sources place the camp precisely, so it is left for review.
results.evidence: Pin 0 North Fork Sauk TH 48.0579,-121.2882 is ~50 m from OSM trailhead node 50625380 (48.05834,-121.28793): correct. Pin 1 White Pass 48.07,-121.17 is ~4.3 km NNW of the pass; USGS GNIS White Pass (id 1528075, Snohomish/Chelan) is 48.03317,-121.14956 and OSM saddle node 3048631504 is 48.03322,-121.14854 (~75 m apart); White Mountain (48.0408,-121.1528) stands immediately north of the pass, consistent. Moved to the GNIS point; USGS ground 5,815 ft -> 5,820. Neighbouring routes already pin White Pass at 48.03317,-121.14955. Pin 2 Boulder Basin Camp 48.105,-121.13: USGS ground there is ~8,115 ft, on the Sitkum Glacier (OSM glacier centroid 48.1105,-121.1305), whereas the camp is at 5,500-6,000 ft at treeline on the ridge south of Sitkum Creek (Sitkum Creek mapped around 48.1116,-121.1656). No source publishes a usable coordinate for the camp (one search snippet gave the summit's own coordinate), so it cannot be placed within 300 m; left, flagged for owner. Pin 3 summit correct. distMi of White Pass (8) not changed; sources put it around 8.9 mi but that was not verified against a primary figure.

results.summary: The saddle pin is already typed as the start of the climbing, so the flagged problem is fixed; but the trailhead pin sits about a mile up the trail rather than where cars park, and no second source pins the parking spot, so it is left for review.
results.evidence: Pins 1 and 2 are both type Base/bivy at 48.19575,-121.65485 (the retype in the finding is already live); that coordinate is the published South Face area coordinate (3,249 ft; USGS ground 3,275 ft). They duplicate each other; not removed because the rules only allow removing pins the route never visits. Pin 0 'Squire Creek Trailhead (Trail #654, end of FS Rd 2040)' 48.2088,-121.6298 (USGS ground ~1,376 ft vs stated 1,900) lies 76 m from the mapped Squire Creek Trail, about 1.3 km up-trail from the mapped old trailhead parking at the road's end (OSM 48.22062,-121.62597, ground ~1,174 ft; a second trail site gives 48.22049,-121.62595 but is derived from the same map data). The pin's own directions say to park at the washout gate; the land manager says the 2002 slide blocks the road two miles before the old trailhead, and the map shows the drivable road ending near 48.2368,-121.6335 with ~2.7 km of abandoned roadbed beyond. The pin is wrong for either reading, but neither the washout parking nor the old trailhead has two independent coordinate sources, and the owner must decide which spot the pin should represent. Summit pin has no coordinates.

results.evidence: Same pins as Doorway Flake. Pins 1 and 2 are both Base/bivy at 48.19575,-121.65485 (the published South Face area coordinate; the saddle is where the Skeena26 approach continues west ~10 minutes to its start) — finding already applied; duplicates left. Pin 0 trailhead 48.2088,-121.6298 is on the trail ~1.3 km beyond the mapped old trailhead (48.22062,-121.62597) and ~3 km beyond where the drivable road ends near 48.2368,-121.6335; its directions describe parking at the washout gate. Only one independent coordinate source exists for either candidate spot, so not moved; owner to decide.
